text.p: Hungary's largest commercial bank OTP summoned its shareholders for September 3 to vote on granting one special rights share to the government to enable it to continue the bank's privatisation.

OTP said in a statement in the Budapest Stock Exchange's official gazette on Friday that the extraordinary meeting should decide on raising the capital by one voting preference share and placing it privately with the Hungarian state.
The share would have a face value of 1,000 forints.
The Hungarian parliament cleared the way in July for the reduction of the state's compulsory holding in certain companies including OTP and the national telecom company Matav.
The legislature amended the privatisation law to allow the state-owned stake in OTP to be reduced to one special rights "golden" share from 25 percent plus one share.
The condition of the reduction is that the state acquires a special rights "golden" share in OTP, by which it will be able to influence the bank's strategic decisions.
OTP traded at 6,650 forints at 1001 GMT, unchanged from Thursday's closing price.
